en fuglekasse.explanation: "En fuglekasse" means "a birdhouse". It is built from "en fugl" (a bird) and "en kasse" (a box). To say birds live in one, use "bo i" (live in): "Fuglene bor i fuglekassen" (The birds live in the birdhouse).

en fugletur.explanation: "En fugletur" means "a birdwatching trip". It is built from "fugl" (bird) and "en tur" (a trip). To say you go for a walk, use "tur" alone: "at gå en tur" (to go for a walk).

en fugleunge.explanation: "En fugleunge" means "a baby bird". It is built from "en fugl" (a bird) and "en unge" (a young one). The last part is also used for the young of other animals: "en andeunge" (a duckling).

en fuldmåne.explanation: "En fuldmåne" means "a full moon". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "en måne" (a moon). To say tonight has one, leave out "en": "I nat er det fuldmåne" (Tonight there is a full moon).

en funktion.explanation: "En funktion" means "a function". To say a machine does not work, use "ude af funktion" (out of order): "Elevatoren er ude af funktion" (The lift is out of order).

en fusion.explanation: "En fusion" means "a merger". It is related to the verb "at fusionere" (to merge): "De to banker fusionerer" (The two banks are merging). When you talk about physics, it means "fusion": "kernefusion" (nuclear fusion).

en fyldning.explanation: "En fyldning" means "a filling". It comes from the verb "at fylde" (to fill). When you talk about food, it means the soft part inside a cake or chocolate: "en fyldning af flødeskum" (a filling of whipped cream).

en fynbo.explanation: "En fynbo" means "a person from Funen". It is built from "Fyn" (Funen) and "-bo" (a resident). The island is called "Fyn" in Danish: "Jeg bor på Fyn" (I live on Funen).

en fyr.explanation: "En fyr" means "a guy". It is a casual word: "Han er en flink fyr" (He is a nice guy). The neutral word is "en mand" (a man): "Der står en mand ved døren" (A man is standing at the door). Do not mix it up with "et fyr" (a lighthouse): "Fyret lyser om natten" (The lighthouse shines at night).

en fyring.explanation: "En fyring" means "a dismissal". It comes from the verb "at fyre" (to fire someone). When you talk about heating a house, "fyring" means "heating": "olie til fyring" (oil for heating).

en fysiker.explanation: "En fysiker" means "a physicist". It comes from "fysik" (physics). To say what someone studies, use "at læse" (to study): "Hun læser fysik" (She studies physics).

en fysioterapeut.explanation: "En fysioterapeut" means "a physiotherapist". To say you go for treatment, use "gå til" (go to): "Jeg går til fysioterapeut hver torsdag" (I go to the physiotherapist every Thursday).

en fåreflok.explanation: "En fåreflok" means "a flock of sheep". It is built from "får" (sheep) and "en flok" (a flock). To talk about a group of people, use "flok" alone: "en flok børn" (a group of children).

en fælde.explanation: "En fælde" means "a trap". When you mean a trap for animals, put the animal first: "en musefælde" (a mousetrap). When you mean a trick set for a person, use "at gå i fælden" (to fall into the trap): "Han gik i fælden" (He fell into the trap).

en fællesspisning.explanation: "En fællesspisning" means "a communal dinner". It is built from "fælles" (shared) and "at spise" (to eat). To invite someone, use "til" (to): "Kom til fællesspisning i aften" (Come to the communal dinner tonight).

en færd.explanation: "En færd" means "a journey / conduct". To say you are in the middle of doing something, use "i færd med at" (in the middle of doing): "Jeg er i færd med at lave mad" (I am in the middle of cooking). To say people are out and about, use "på færde" (about): "Der er tyve på færde" (There are thieves about).

en færdighed.explanation: "En færdighed" means "a skill". It is built from "færdig" (finished, ready). To say what someone is good at, use "færdigheder i" (skills in): "Hun har gode færdigheder i matematik" (She has good skills in maths).

en færdselsregel.explanation: "En færdselsregel" means "a traffic rule". It is built from "færdsel" (traffic) and "en regel" (a rule). To say someone breaks the rules, use "at overtræde" (to break): "Han overtrådte færdselsreglerne" (He broke the traffic rules).

en færge.explanation: "En færge" means "a ferry". To say you travel by ferry, use "med" (by): "Vi sejler med færgen til Bornholm" (We sail by ferry to Bornholm).

en fætter.explanation: "En fætter" means "a male cousin". Danish has a separate word for a female cousin, "en kusine": "Min kusine bor i Odense" (My female cousin lives in Odense).

en fødegang.explanation: "En fødegang" means "a maternity ward". It comes from the verb "at føde" (to give birth). To say where a woman is, use "på" (in): "Hun er på fødegangen" (She is in the maternity ward).

en fødevare.explanation: "En fødevare" means "a food item". It is built from "føde" (food) and "en vare" (a product). The Danish food authority is called "Fødevarestyrelsen" (the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration).

en fødsel.explanation: "En fødsel" means "a birth". It comes from the verb "at føde" (to give birth). It is also the first part of "fødselsdag" (birthday): "Min fødselsdag er i maj" (My birthday is in May).

en fødselsdag.explanation: "En fødselsdag" means "a birthday". It is built from "en fødsel" (a birth) and "en dag" (a day). To say it is your birthday, use "have" (to have): "Jeg har fødselsdag" (literally, "I have birthday"). To congratulate someone, say: "Tillykke med fødselsdagen!" (Happy birthday!)

en fødselsdagsfest.explanation: "En fødselsdagsfest" means "a birthday party". It is built from "fødselsdag" (birthday) and "en fest" (a party). To invite someone, use "at invitere til" (to invite to): "Jeg inviterer dig til fødselsdagsfest" (I invite you to a birthday party).
